context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Stop serialising the whole user model. Replace `res.json({ user })` with an explicit allow-list response shape, for example `const publicUser = toPublicUser(user);` followed by `res.json({ user: publicUser });`. Define `toPublicUser` once, returning only the fields this endpoint's requester is entitled to see (such as id, display name, and an email only when the requester is the user or an authorised role). Exclude secrets and internal fields such as password hashes, tokens, MFA secrets, internal flags, and nested relations unless the response needs them. Use that same serializer on every route that returns this user record, so access limits are enforced consistently. Add a test that asserts sensitive fields are absent from the response and that the field set matches the allow-list for each requester role.
